title: Maple Syrup vs Sugar: Which Actually Contains More Sugar?

seo.title: Maple Syrup vs Sugar: Which Has More?
seo.meta_description: Granulated sugar is nearly 100% sugar by weight, while pure maple syrup is about 60–67% sugars because it contains water. By the tablespoon, however, their sugar and calorie totals can be surprisingly close.
seo.search_intent: Compare maple syrup and granulated sugar by weight and by household serving to resolve which is more concentrated.

excerpt: Granulated sugar is far more concentrated by weight: nearly 100 g sugar per 100 g versus roughly 60–67 g in pure maple syrup. A tablespoon tells a different story because the syrup serving weighs more.
content_html:
Maple syrup is diluted with its own water, while granulated sugar is essentially dry sucrose. So by weight, granulated sugar clearly contains more sugar. By the tablespoon, the gap becomes much smaller because a spoonful of syrup weighs more.

Per 100 grams, granulated sugar is much more concentrated

Per 100 gTotal sugarsCalories
Granulated sugar≈100 g≈387 kcal
Pure maple syrup≈60–67 g≈260 kcal

Roughly one-third of maple syrup is water, which lowers both sugar and calorie concentration. It is still a concentrated sweetener, not a low-sugar food.

A tablespoon nearly erases the calorie gap

A tablespoon of maple syrup weighs about 20 grams and commonly supplies around 50–55 calories with roughly 12–13 grams of sugar. A level tablespoon of granulated sugar weighs closer to 12–13 grams and provides roughly 48–50 calories and about the same number of grams of sugar.

That is why both statements can be true: syrup has much less sugar per 100 grams, yet a spoonful used at the table can deliver a very similar sugar load.

Maple's micronutrients do not cancel its added sugar

Pure maple syrup contains small amounts of manganese, riboflavin, and other compounds that refined white sugar largely lacks. Those extras can distinguish the foods, but nutritionally maple syrup still functions mainly as an added-sugar sweetener.

Baking swaps change the liquid balance

Replacing dry sugar with syrup also adds water and maple flavor. Cakes and cookies may need liquid adjustments, and browning can change, so a cup-for-cup substitution is not only a nutrition question.

If the comparison is per gram, granulated sugar wins by a wide margin. If it is one tablespoon of each, they are much closer than the liquid-versus-crystal appearance suggests.

faq.question: Does maple syrup have less sugar than white sugar?
faq.answer: Per 100 grams, yes, because maple syrup contains substantial water. Per tablespoon, the amount of sugar can be quite similar because syrup is denser and the spoonful weighs more.

faq.question: Is maple syrup lower in calories?
faq.answer: Per 100 grams it is lower, around 260 kcal versus about 387 kcal for granulated sugar. Per tablespoon, both are around 50 calories.

faq.question: Is maple syrup an added sugar?
faq.answer: Yes. When used to sweeten foods, pure maple syrup contributes added sugars even though it also contains small amounts of micronutrients.
